title: The Agentic Garden of Forking Paths
one_liner: 用不同先验立场的智能体记录并审查替代分析，以 m-value 衡量一项报告结果在指定分析分布中有多极端。
classification_reason: 研究同一数据与问题下的分析选择、立场偏差和结果分布，归入兴趣探索。跨学科案例用于检验分析行为，不据此强行划入某个科学领域的 Agent benchmark。

problem.text: 同一份数据和研究问题，往往允许多种可辩护的分析。作者研究先验立场怎样影响智能体探索和报告的结果，以及只检查最终报告为何可能漏掉选择性报告。实验涉及移民与福利支持、咖啡与健康、社交媒体与青少年心理健康、肠道菌群与 BMI 四个问题。

gap.text: 传统多分析者研究主要观察最终答案，难以区分探索过程与最后选结果各自带来的偏差；人工多路径分析又依赖研究者事先列举选择。单个分析的 p-value 处理既定分析下的抽样不确定性，不能说明换一条分析路径后结论会怎样。

method.text: 主实验固定数据、问题、模型和预算，仅改变先验立场。每个问题设两个相反 persona，各运行 20 次 Claude Code／Sonnet 4.6；每次连续 10 轮、每轮拟合 10 个候选方案，保留历史，最后选一个作为主结论。Sonnet 4.6 先检查并修正推断，独立 Codex／GPT-5.4 再判断是否存在重大方法错误。Agentic Bootstrap 另加入中立 persona，汇集各轮候选方案，经质控和审查构建参考分布 Π。固定数据，令 T 为效应值或 Z 统计量，双侧 m(t₀;Π)=2×min{PΠ(T≤t₀), PΠ(T≥t₀)}；实际用保留方案的比例估计。

trace.text: 移民案例使用 ISSP 五轮调查，覆盖 1985—2016 年约 15.3 万名受访者。智能体可更换福利指标、移民指标、模型、样本、时期、变量构造与控制项。赞成、反对、中立三种 persona 各运行 20 次，共产生约 6,000 个候选方案，审查后留下 4,392 个。作者据此计算 42 个人类团队的 897 份分析报告在参考分布中的 m-value，比较报告是否集中于分布尾部。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入是数据、研究问题、persona 与固定分析及审查协议；输出包括各轮代码、候选模型结果、主结论和复现脚本。聚合候选分析后得到规格曲线、m-value 和中央 95% 的分析结果区间。这里的区间描述分析选择带来的结果变化，不是某一固定参数的传统置信区间。

results.text: 四个问题共 160 次主实验，137 次（86%）通过 AI 审查。人工抽查 40 份，每份由 3 人评审，31 份（78%）获多数通过；AI 与人类多数意见一致率为 70%。移民案例中 AI 的立场间效应差为 0.020，人类为 0.028，约复现其 72%；置乱数据、更换 harness 和固定估计目标后仍观察到立场差异。以 4,392 个方案为参照，13.5% 的人类报告满足 m<0.05；在人类 p<0.05 的报告中，该比例为 40%。改用 Codex／GPT-5.4 构建参照时，m-value 排名相关为 0.93，m<0.05 分类一致率为 93%。

contributions.text: 作者将偏差分为两个可观察环节：探索逐渐偏向支持先验的方案，最终选择又进一步放大这种倾向。Agentic Bootstrap 把全轨迹中的候选分析转成可复用的参照，m-value 则刻画报告相对该参照的尾部位置。附录给出校准、一致性和方法区间覆盖性质；校准要求报告来自同一声明的方法分布，并满足连续性等条件。

limitations.text: 参考分布由模型、persona、提示词和审查规则共同决定，并非所有合理分析的均匀样本。审查主要依据结构化分析说明；人工评审平均两两 AC1 为 0.30，不能把通过审查等同于客观正确。知识库分析：m-value 小只说明相对指定参照较极端，不能单独证明造假；m-value 大也不能证明因果结论正确或所有合理方法一致。同一次运行的候选分析相关，论文按运行重采样估计不确定性，不能将 4,392 个方案都当作独立抽样。

cost.text: 论文报告每次约 100 个候选方案的分析耗时约 15 分钟、花费约 1.68 美元，平均每方案约 0.016 美元；移民问题的整套参考分布约 100 美元，可供多个报告复用。该报价未单独拆出人工审查及每个审查环节的成本，不能视为包含人工的完整成本。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：归入兴趣探索，关注分析自由度与科学报告的可信度。与 Branchpoint 相互补充：这里通过不同 persona 的独立分析建立参照并计算 m-value；Branchpoint 复用轨迹前缀、干预决策以探索更多分支，主要考察数值多样性与成本。

related.reason: 都探索同一数据与问题下的多条分析路径。Agentic Bootstrap 汇集不同 persona 的独立分析，经过方法审查构建参照并计算 m-value；Branchpoint 从轨迹决策点分叉，以新颖性筛选分支，研究多样性和成本。

en.one_liner: Persona-conditioned agents log and review alternative analyses; the m-value measures how extreme a reported claim is within a declared analysis-space distribution.

sections.problem: The same data and question can admit several defensible analyses. The paper studies how prior beliefs shape agents’ exploration and reported findings, and why inspecting only the final report can miss selective reporting. Experiments cover immigration and welfare support, coffee and health, social media and adolescent mental health, and the gut microbiome and BMI.
sections.gap: Human many-analyst studies typically observe final answers, making exploration and final selection difficult to separate. Manual multiverse analysis requires investigators to enumerate choices beforehand. A p-value addresses sampling uncertainty conditional on a selected analysis, rather than the variation produced by choosing another analysis path.
sections.method: The main experiment fixes the data, question, model and budget while varying prior beliefs. Each question has two opposing personas with 20 Claude Code/Sonnet 4.6 runs each. A run fits ten candidates in each of ten history-aware rounds and selects one headline result. Sonnet 4.6 first audits and repairs inference; an independent Codex/GPT-5.4 reviewer screens for major methodological errors. Agentic Bootstrap adds a neutral persona and pools candidates across rounds, retaining quality-controlled and review-passing specifications as reference distribution Π. For fixed data and a claim statistic T, such as an effect estimate or Z-statistic, the two-sided definition is m(t₀;Π)=2×min{PΠ(T≤t₀), PΠ(T≥t₀)}, estimated using retained specifications.
sections.trace: The immigration example uses five ISSP waves from 1985–2016 with roughly 153,000 respondents. Agents vary outcomes, immigration measures, models, samples, periods, variable construction and controls. Twenty runs for each of pro, anti and neutral personas yield roughly 6,000 candidates, of which 4,392 survive review. This reference is used to calculate m-values for 897 human specifications from 42 teams and examine their concentration in the tails.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs are data, a research question, personas, and fixed analysis and review protocols. Outputs include round-level code, candidate-model results, a headline finding and a reproduction script. Pooling candidates yields a specification curve, m-values and a central 95% interval over analysis results. This interval describes variation across analytical choices, not a conventional confidence interval for a single fixed parameter.
sections.results: Across four questions and 160 main runs, 137 (86%) passed AI review. In a human subsample of 40 analyses rated by three reviewers each, 31 (78%) passed by majority; AI agreed with that majority on 70%. The immigration effect-estimate gap was 0.020 for agents versus 0.028 for humans, reproducing approximately 72% of the human gap. Persona gaps persisted with permuted data, another harness and a fixed estimand. Relative to the 4,392-specification reference, 13.5% of human reports had m<0.05; among human reports with p<0.05, the share was 40%. Rebuilding the reference with Codex/GPT-5.4 gave m-value rank correlation 0.93 and 93% agreement on m<0.05 classifications.
sections.contributions: The paper separates two observable sources of bias: exploration progressively favors belief-aligned specifications, and final selection amplifies the divergence. Agentic Bootstrap converts logged candidates into a reusable reference; the m-value measures a report’s tail position relative to that reference. The appendix establishes calibration, consistency and method-interval coverage under stated assumptions, including a common declared method distribution and continuity for calibration.
sections.limitations: The reference depends on models, personas, prompts and review rules; it is not a uniform sample of every reasonable analysis. Review largely uses structured specification summaries, and mean human pairwise AC1 was 0.30. Passing review is not proof of correctness. Library interpretation: a small m-value indicates extremeness relative to the declared reference, not proof of misconduct; a large value proves neither causal validity nor agreement across all reasonable methods. Candidates within a run are dependent. The paper resamples runs to estimate uncertainty rather than treating all 4,392 specifications as independent draws.
sections.cost: The paper reports roughly 15 minutes and $1.68 per run generating about 100 specifications, or approximately $0.016 per specification. The immigration reference costs about $100 and can serve multiple reported claims. Human-review costs and individual review-stage costs are not separately itemized, so this is not a complete accounting including human labor.
sections.relevance: Library analysis: placed in Other interests for its study of analytical flexibility and scientific reporting. It complements Branchpoint: persona-conditioned independent analyses construct a reference and m-values here, whereas Branchpoint reuses trajectory prefixes and intervenes on decisions to explore branches, emphasizing numerical diversity and cost.

related.branchpoint: Both explore alternative analyses for fixed data and a question. Agentic Bootstrap pools persona-conditioned independent analyses, applies methodological review and calculates m-values; Branchpoint forks trajectory decisions, screens for novelty and studies diversity and cost.
